questions.question_text: Write $0.\overline{65}$ as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Used $\frac{65}{100}$ and simplified, treating the decimal as terminating rather than recurring.
Used one $9$ although the repeating block has two digits.
Placed only the first repeating digit over $9$ instead of the whole two-digit block over $99$.

questions.solution_text:
A two-digit block repeats, so it sits over $99$.
$0.\overline{65}=\frac{65}{99}$
This fraction is already in simplest form.

options.why: Ignored the dot and converted the terminating decimal $0.2$ instead.
Used the two-digit-block denominator $99$ although only one digit repeats.
Wrote the $9$ as the numerator and the repeating digit as the denominator, inverting the fraction.

questions.solution_text:
One digit repeats, so it sits over a single $9$.
$0.\dot{2}=\frac{2}{9}$

questions.question_text: Write $0.\overline{54}$ as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Simplified $\frac{54}{100}$, treating the decimal as terminating rather than recurring.
Used three $9$s although the repeating block has only two digits.
Placed only the first repeating digit over $9$ instead of the whole two-digit block over $99$.

questions.solution_text:
A two-digit block repeats, so it sits over $99$.
$0.\overline{54}=\frac{54}{99}$
$=\frac{6}{11}$

questions.question_text: Use a calculator to write $\frac{5}{6}$ as a decimal, in recurring decimal notation.

options.why: Barred both digits, although the $8$ appears once and only the $3$ repeats.
Rounded the calculator display to two decimal places instead of marking the recurring digit.
Placed the dot over the $8$, which does not repeat, rather than over the $3$.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{5}{6}$
$=0.83333\ldots$
Only the $3$ repeats, so the dot goes over the $3$ alone.
$\frac{5}{6}=0.8\dot{3}$

questions.question_text: Write $0.2\dot{7}$ as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Treated both digits as the repeating block, although the $2$ appears only once.
Used the correct denominator $90$ but forgot to subtract the non-repeating digit from $27$.
Converted only the repeating digit and dropped the $2$ tenths altogether.

questions.question_text: Write $5.\overline{27}$ as a mixed numeral in simplest form.

options.why: Treated the decimal as the terminating $5.27$ and used hundredths place value.
Wrote the two repeating digits as the fraction $\frac{2}{7}$ instead of placing them over $99$.
Converted the decimal part correctly but dropped the whole-number part $5$.

questions.solution_text:
Keep the whole-number part and convert only the decimal part.
$0.\overline{27}=\frac{27}{99}$
$=\frac{3}{11}$
$5.\overline{27}=5\frac{3}{11}$

questions.question_text:
A calculator shows $\frac{7}{9}=0.7777778$.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The exact value is $0.\dot{7}$; the calculator has rounded its last displayed digit up.
The exact value is $0.7777778$, because that is what the calculator shows.
options.why: Treats a rounded display as the exact value, when the display simply runs out of room.

options.text: The exact value is $0.\overline{78}$, because the display ends in $78$.
options.why: Reads the rounded final digit as part of the repeating block, making a two-digit block that does not exist.

options.text: $\frac{7}{9}$ is irrational, because its decimal never ends.
options.why: Confuses a recurring decimal with a non-terminating, non-recurring one; a repeating decimal is always rational.

questions.solution_text:
The display holds a fixed number of digits, so the last $7$ was rounded up to an $8$.
Dividing $7$ by $9$ repeats the digit $7$ forever.
$\frac{7}{9}=0.\dot{7}$

questions.question_text: Without using a calculator, convert $0.\overline{26}$ to a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Used $\frac{26}{100}$ and simplified, treating the decimal as terminating rather than recurring.
Used $9$ as the denominator instead of $99$ for a two-digit repeating block.
Converted only the first repeating digit and dropped the $6$ from the repeating block.

questions.solution_text:
Let $x=0.262626\ldots$
A two-digit block repeats, so multiply by $100$.
$100x=26.262626\ldots$
$100x-x=26.262626\ldots-0.262626\ldots$
$99x=26$
$x=\frac{26}{99}$
This fraction is already in simplest form.

questions.question_text: Write $0.4\overline{36}$ as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Placed all three digits over $999$, ignoring that the $4$ appears only once.
Subtracted the non-repeating digit correctly but divided by $999$ instead of $990$.
Used the correct denominator $990$ but forgot to subtract the non-repeating digit from $436$.
